AlCoCrFeNi2:4 HEA ingots were obtained using vacuum arc remelting (V AR) under a 3 /C2 10/C0 4mbar vacuum. Elements with over 99 wt.% purity were utilized as raw materials. Four consecutive remelting procedures were performed to improve the chemical homogeneity of the ingots
The alloy /C213s final thickness of 0.75 mm was achieved through seven passes of cold rolling, i.e., 90% re-duction.
After cold rolling, the specimens were cut into dog-bone specimens using Wire Electrical Discharge Machining (WEDM) and per JISSZ2201, as shown in Fig. 1.

A combination of FCC and BCC dual phases was present in the as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2:4 alloy. It is evident that the intensity of the FCC phase is higher than that of the BCC phase, indicating that the volume fraction of the FCC phase is higher than that of the BCC phase.

A combination of FCC and BCC dual phases was present in the as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2:4 alloy. It is evident that the intensity of the FCC phase is higher than that of the BCC phase, indicating that the volume fraction of the FCC phase is higher than that of the BCC phase.
There are two distinct phases in the as-cast structure. Dendritic regions include a L1 2(FCC) phase and a B2(BCC) phase formed within the interdendritic structure.

Figure 3(a) and (b) illustrates the specimen /C213s microstructure in an as-cast state, demonstrating a typical dendritic structure. The microstructure comprises interdendritic (ID) and cellular-like dendrite regions (DR).

By cold rolling up to 90% of the thickness, the hardness can be increased by almost 60%. This behavior occurs as a result of dislocation density variations due to strain hardening during cold rolling.

In the cold rolling condition, the alloy /C213s yield and ultimate strengths increased signiﬁcantly compared to the as-cast state. Nonetheless, this was accomplished at the expense of ductility.
The tensile yield strength in the as-cast and cold-rolled states was approximately 831 and 1791 MPa, respectively.
